-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension.Constructions

/-!
# Bases adapted to a finite filtration

This file assembles bases of the successive quotients of an increasing
filtration into a basis of a finite filtration stage.  It also records the
chosen representative of every graded basis vector in the stage where that
vector is introduced.

## Main declarations

* `Module.Basis.FiltrationIndex` is the dependent sum of the graded basis
  indices below a finite cutoff.
* `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStage` is the resulting basis of a finite
  filtration stage.
* `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStageVector` regards a basis vector as an element
  of the stage where it is introduced.
* `Module.Basis.ofFiltration` specializes the construction when the final
  stage is the whole ambient module.

## Informal proof

Let `F 0 <= F 1 <= ...` be a filtration with `F 0 = 0`, and suppose that the
quotient `F (i+1) / F i` has a basis indexed by `kappa i`.  We argue by
induction on the cutoff `n`.

For `n = 0`, the stage `F 0` is the zero module, so its empty family is a
basis.  For the induction step, identify `F n` with its image as a submodule
of `F (n+1)`.  Mathlib's `Module.Basis.sumQuot` combines the transported basis
of this submodule with arbitrary representatives of the supplied basis of
`F (n+1) / F n`.  Its index type is the disjoint sum of the old indices and
`kappa n`; reindexing by the evident equivalence identifies this sum with
`Sigma i : Fin (n+1), kappa i`.

The `sumQuot_inl` formula says that every old vector is carried forward
without changing its ambient value.  The `sumQuot_inr` formula says that each
new vector maps to the prescribed quotient-basis vector.  Induction therefore
shows that every final basis vector still lies in the stage where it was
introduced and has exactly the prescribed image in the corresponding
successive quotient.  If the final stage is the top submodule, its canonical
linear equivalence with the ambient module transports this stage basis to a
basis of the ambient module without changing any underlying vector.
-/

@[expose] public section

universe u v w

namespace Module.Basis

variable {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R]
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

/-- The dependent sum of the graded basis indices strictly below `n`. -/
abbrev FiltrationIndex (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) :=
  Σ i : Fin n, κ i.val

/-- Add the last graded index to the dependent sum of the preceding indices. -/
def filtrationIndexSuccEquiv (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) :
    FiltrationIndex κ n ⊕ κ n ≃ FiltrationIndex κ (n + 1) where
  toFun
    | Sum.inl ⟨i, a⟩ => ⟨i.castSucc, a⟩
    | Sum.inr a => ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩
  invFun p :=
    Fin.lastCases (fun a => Sum.inr a)
      (fun i a => Sum.inl ⟨i, a⟩) p.1 p.2
  left_inv x := by
    rcases x with (⟨i, a⟩ | a)
    · simp
    · simp
  right_inv p := by
    rcases p with ⟨i, a⟩
    revert a
    refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun j => ?_) i
    · intro a
      simp
    · intro a
      simp

@[simp]
theorem filtrationIndexSuccEquiv_apply_inl
    (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n (Sum.inl ⟨i, a⟩) = ⟨i.castSucc, a⟩ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem filtrationIndexSuccEquiv_apply_inr
    (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) (a : κ n) :
    filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n (Sum.inr a) = ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩ :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem filtrationIndexSuccEquiv_symm_castSucc
    (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    (filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n).symm ⟨i.castSucc, a⟩ =
      Sum.inl ⟨i, a⟩ := by
  simp [filtrationIndexSuccEquiv]

@[simp]
theorem filtrationIndexSuccEquiv_symm_last
    (κ : ℕ → Type w) (n : ℕ) (a : κ n) :
    (filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n).symm ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩ =
      Sum.inr a := by
  simp [filtrationIndexSuccEquiv]

/-- A basis of a finite filtration stage assembled from bases of all its
successive quotients.

The filtration is indexed by natural numbers, while `n` selects the finite
segment used by this construction.  The result is indexed by the dependent
sum of the supplied graded basis indices. -/
noncomputable def ofFiltrationStage
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w) :
    ∀ n,
      (∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1)) →
      (∀ i : Fin n,
        Basis (κ i.val) R
          (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype)) →
      Basis (FiltrationIndex κ n) R (F n)
  | 0, _, _ => by
      letI : Subsingleton (F 0) := by
        rw [hzero]
        infer_instance
      exact Basis.empty (F 0)
  | n + 1, hF, b =>
      let hF' : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1) :=
        fun i => hF i.castSucc
      let b' : ∀ i : Fin n,
          Basis (κ i.val) R
            (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype) :=
        fun i => b i.castSucc
      let hlast : F n ≤ F (n + 1) := by
        simpa using hF (Fin.last n)
      let blast : Basis (κ n) R
          (F (n + 1) ⧸ (F n).comap (F (n + 1)).subtype) := by
        simpa using b (Fin.last n)
      let lower : Basis (FiltrationIndex κ n) R
          ((F n).comap (F (n + 1)).subtype) :=
        (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF' b').map
          (Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe hlast).symm
      (lower.sumQuot blast).reindex (filtrationIndexSuccEquiv κ n)

/-- Passing to the next filtration stage does not change an earlier basis
vector as an element of the ambient module. -/
@[simp]
theorem ofFiltrationStage_castSucc
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ) (hF : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), F j.val ≤ F (j.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1),
      Basis (κ j.val) R
        (F (j.val + 1) ⧸ (F j.val).comap (F (j.val + 1)).subtype))
    (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ (n + 1) hF b
        ⟨i.castSucc, a⟩ : F (n + 1)) : M) =
      (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n (fun j => hF j.castSucc)
        (fun j => b j.castSucc) ⟨i, a⟩ : F n) := by
  simp [ofFiltrationStage]

/-- The vector added at the last step maps to the prescribed basis vector of
the last successive quotient. -/
@[simp]
theorem ofFiltrationStage_last_mk
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1),
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (a : κ n) :
    Submodule.Quotient.mk
        (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ (n + 1) hF b ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩) =
      b (Fin.last n) a := by
  simp [ofFiltrationStage]

/-- Every assembled basis vector belongs to the filtration stage where its
graded index is introduced. -/
theorem ofFiltrationStage_mem
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ) (hF : ∀ j : Fin n, F j.val ≤ F (j.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ j : Fin n,
      Basis (κ j.val) R
        (F (j.val + 1) ⧸ (F j.val).comap (F (j.val + 1)).subtype))
    (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b ⟨i, a⟩ : F n) : M) ∈
      F (i.val + 1) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact Fin.elim0 i
  | succ n ih =>
      revert a
      refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun j => ?_) i
      · intro a
        exact (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ (n + 1) hF b
          ⟨Fin.last n, a⟩).property
      · intro a
        rw [ofFiltrationStage_castSucc]
        exact ih (fun k => hF k.castSucc) (fun k => b k.castSucc) j a

/-- An assembled basis vector, restricted to the filtration stage where it
is introduced. -/
noncomputable def ofFiltrationStageVector
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) : F (i.val + 1) :=
  ⟨ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b ⟨i, a⟩,
    ofFiltrationStage_mem F hzero κ n hF b i a⟩

/-- Every assembled filtration vector is an exact representative of the
supplied basis vector in its successive quotient. -/
@[simp]
theorem ofFiltrationStageVector_mk
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (i : Fin n) (a : κ i.val) :
    Submodule.Quotient.mk
        (ofFiltrationStageVector F hzero κ n hF b i a) = b i a := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact Fin.elim0 i
  | succ n ih =>
      revert a
      refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun j => ?_) i
      · intro a
        simp [ofFiltrationStageVector]
      · intro a
        simpa [ofFiltrationStageVector] using
          ih (fun k => hF k.castSucc) (fun k => b k.castSucc) j a

/-- A basis of the ambient module assembled from bases of the successive
quotients of a finite filtration from zero to the top submodule. -/
noncomputable def ofFiltration
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤) : Basis (FiltrationIndex κ n) R M :=
  (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b).map
    ((LinearEquiv.ofEq (F n) ⊤ htop).trans Submodule.topEquiv)

/-- Mapping the final filtration stage to the ambient module does not change
the underlying basis vectors. -/
@[simp]
theorem ofFiltration_apply
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥) (κ : ℕ → Type w)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤) (p : FiltrationIndex κ n) :
    ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop p =
      (ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b p : F n) := by
  simp [ofFiltration]

end Module.Basis

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Determinant

/-!
# Determinants along finite invariant filtrations

This file packages and iterates the determinant factorization for an
endomorphism preserving a submodule.  It is intended for finite filtrations
whose stages and successive quotients are finite free modules.

## Main declarations

* `LinearMap.InvariantExtension` records one inclusion of a filtration stage
  as an invariant submodule of the next stage.
* `LinearMap.InvariantExtension.quotientMap` is the induced endomorphism on
  the successive quotient.
* `LinearMap.InvariantExtension.det_eq_det_mul_det_quotientMap` is the
  one-step determinant factorization.
* `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded` iterates the factorization through a
  finite tower.
* `LinearMap.det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton` removes the bottom
  determinant when the initial stage is zero.

## Informal proof

For one step, let `f` act on the lower stage `V`, let `g` act on the next
stage `W`, and identify `V` with a `g`-invariant submodule `S` of `W`.
Mathlib's `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det` chooses a basis of `S`, extends it by
a basis of `W/S`, and writes the matrix of `g` in block upper-triangular
form.  It gives

`det(g) = det(g|S) * det(g on W/S)`.

The stored intertwining equality says that `g|S` is conjugate to `f` through
the identification `V ~= S`.  Determinants are invariant under conjugation,
so the first factor is `det(f)`.

For a finite tower, apply this one-step identity at every adjacent pair.  A
plain induction over `Fin n` multiplies the successive quotient determinants:
if `d_(i+1) = d_i * q_i`, then

`d_n = d_0 * product_i q_i`.

When the bottom stage is a zero module, its determinant is one, leaving only
the product over the graded quotients.

The freeness of every successive quotient is explicit.  Over an arbitrary
commutative ring it does not follow merely from freeness of the two adjacent
stages; this hypothesis is therefore not hidden or weakened.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators

universe u v w

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
variable {V : Type v} {W : Type w}
variable [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V]
variable [AddCommGroup W] [Module R W]

/-- One step of an invariant filtration.

The lower endomorphism `f` is identified with the restriction of the upper
endomorphism `g` to `submodule`.  The quotient endomorphism is consequently
the action of `g` on the corresponding successive graded piece. -/
structure InvariantExtension (f : V →ₗ[R] V) (g : W →ₗ[R] W) where
  /-- The lower filtration stage inside the next stage. -/
  submodule : Submodule R W
  /-- The next-stage endomorphism preserves the lower stage. -/
  stable : submodule ≤ submodule.comap g
  /-- Identification of the abstract lower stage with the invariant
  submodule. -/
  equiv : V ≃ₗ[R] submodule
  /-- Under `equiv`, the lower endomorphism intertwines with the restriction
  of the upper endomorphism. -/
  intertwines :
    (equiv : V →ₗ[R] submodule) ∘ₗ f =
      (g.restrict stable) ∘ₗ (equiv : V →ₗ[R] submodule)

namespace InvariantExtension

variable {f : V →ₗ[R] V} {g : W →ₗ[R] W}

/-- The intertwining square in an invariant extension, rewritten as a
conjugation identity. -/
theorem conjugate_eq (E : InvariantExtension f g) :
    (E.equiv : V →ₗ[R] E.submodule) ∘ₗ f ∘ₗ
        (E.equiv.symm : E.submodule →ₗ[R] V) =
      g.restrict E.stable := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  have h := LinearMap.congr_fun E.intertwines (E.equiv.symm x)
  simpa using h

/-- The endomorphism induced on the successive quotient of an invariant
extension. -/
def quotientMap (E : InvariantExtension f g) :
    (W ⧸ E.submodule) →ₗ[R] (W ⧸ E.submodule) :=
  E.submodule.mapQ E.submodule g E.stable

/-- The quotient endomorphism sends the class of a representative to the
class of its image under the upper-stage endomorphism. -/
@[simp]
theorem quotientMap_mk (E : InvariantExtension f g) (x : W) :
    E.quotientMap (Submodule.Quotient.mk x : W ⧸ E.submodule) =
      (Submodule.Quotient.mk (g x) : W ⧸ E.submodule) := by
  simpa only [quotientMap] using
    (Submodule.mapQ_apply E.submodule E.submodule g (h := E.stable) x)

/-- Determinant factorization for one invariant extension.

This is the reusable one-step block-triangular formula.  The lower stage and
the quotient are required to be finite free in exactly the places needed by
`LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det`. -/
theorem det_eq_det_mul_det_quotientMap (E : InvariantExtension f g)
    [Module.Free R V] [Module.Finite R V] [Module.Finite R W]
    [Module.Free R (W ⧸ E.submodule)] :
    g.det = f.det * E.quotientMap.det := by
  let _ : Module.Free R E.submodule := Module.Free.of_equiv E.equiv
  let _ : Module.Finite R E.submodule := Module.Finite.equiv E.equiv
  calc
    g.det = (g.restrict E.stable).det * E.quotientMap.det :=
      g.det_eq_det_mul_det E.submodule E.stable
    _ = f.det * E.quotientMap.det := by
      rw [← E.conjugate_eq, LinearMap.det_conj]

end InvariantExtension

private theorem last_eq_first_mul_prod {n : ℕ} (d : Fin (n + 1) → R)
    (q : Fin n → R) (h : ∀ i, d i.succ = d i.castSucc * q i) :
    d (Fin.last n) = d 0 * ∏ i, q i := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      have hprefix :
          d (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) =
            d 0 * ∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc := by
        apply ih (d := fun i ↦ d i.castSucc) (q := fun i ↦ q i.castSucc)
        intro i
        simpa using h i.castSucc
      calc
        d (Fin.last (n + 1)) =
            d (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) * q (Fin.last n) := by
          simpa using h (Fin.last n)
        _ = (d 0 * ∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc) * q (Fin.last n) := by
          rw [hprefix]
        _ = d 0 * ((∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc) * q (Fin.last n)) := by
          rw [mul_assoc]
        _ = d 0 * ∏ i, q i := by
          rw [Fin.prod_univ_castSucc]

section FiniteTower

variable {n : ℕ} {M : Fin (n + 1) → Type v}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- The determinant on the final stage of a finite invariant filtration is
the determinant on the initial stage times the product of the determinants
on all successive graded quotients.

The stages may be presented as different module types.  Each `step i`
identifies stage `i` with an invariant submodule of stage `i+1`; this avoids
choosing coercion-heavy nested subtypes and makes the theorem convenient for
filtrations transported through canonical linear equivalences. -/
theorem det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule)) :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det =
      (endomorphism 0).det * ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.det := by
  refine last_eq_first_mul_prod
    (d := fun i ↦ (endomorphism i).det)
    (q := fun i ↦ (step i).quotientMap.det) ?_
  intro i
  let _ : Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule) := quotientFree i
  exact (step i).det_eq_det_mul_det_quotientMap

/-- Version of `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded` for a filtration whose
bottom determinant has already been identified with one. -/
theorem det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_det_eq_one
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule))
    (hbottom : (endomorphism 0).det = 1) :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det = ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.det := by
  rw [det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded endomorphism step quotientFree, hbottom, one_mul]

/-- Determinant product formula for a finite invariant filtration starting
at a zero module. -/
theorem det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule))
    [Subsingleton (M 0)] :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det = ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.det :=
  det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_det_eq_one endomorphism step quotientFree
    (LinearMap.det_eq_one_of_subsingleton _)

end FiniteTower

end LinearMap

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Basis.FiniteFiltration
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Determinant.FiniteFiltration

/-!
# Determinants of filtration-unipotent endomorphisms

Let

```text
F 0 ≤ F 1 ≤ ... ≤ F n = M
```

be a finite filtration from zero to the whole module.  Choose a basis of
every successive quotient and assemble them into
`Module.Basis.ofFiltration`.  This file proves that an endomorphism has
determinant one if it fixes every assembled graded basis vector modulo the
preceding stage.

More precisely, write `B` for the assembled basis and suppose

```text
U (B ⟨i,a⟩) - B ⟨i,a⟩ ∈ F i
```

for every grade `i` and graded basis index `a`.  Then `U.det = 1`.

## Informal proof

### Prefix agreement

For `j ≤ n`, an index `i : Fin j` also defines an index of the final
assembled basis.  Repeated use of `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStage_castSucc`
shows that the `i`-th vector of the stage-`j` basis and the corresponding
ambient vector have the same underlying element of `M`.  The proof is by
induction on the final cutoff.  At a successor cutoff, either `j` is already
below the previous cutoff, in which case apply the induction hypothesis and
one cast-successor identity, or `j` is the new final cutoff, in which case
the statement is reflexive.

### Derived stage stability

Fix `j ≤ n` and expand `x : F j` in the explicit basis
`ofFiltrationStage ... j`.  For a basis vector introduced in grade `i < j`,
prefix agreement identifies its ambient value with `B ⟨i,a⟩`.  The
hypothesis places its error under `U` in `F i`, hence in `F j`; the vector
itself already belongs to `F j`.  Thus its image under `U` belongs to `F j`.
Linearity and the finite basis expansion prove `F j ≤ (F j).comap U`.

### Adjacent quotients

Restrict `U` to every stable stage.  For adjacent stages, identify `F i`
with its copy inside `F (i+1)` by
`Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe`.  The restricted maps intertwine on
underlying values, producing a `LinearMap.InvariantExtension`.

The quotient basis vector `b i a` is represented by
`Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStageVector ... i a`.  Its ambient value is exactly
the assembled grade-`i` basis vector.  The error hypothesis therefore says
that the induced quotient map fixes this representative modulo `F i`.
Basis extensionality proves that every successive quotient map is
`LinearMap.id`; its determinant is one.

### Determinant product

The explicit stage bases and quotient bases install finite-free structures
on all modules used by
`LinearMap.det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton`.  The bottom equality
`F 0 = ⊥` makes the first stage subsingleton.  The determinant product is
therefore a product of ones.  Finally, the canonical equivalence `F n ≃ M`
conjugates the last restricted endomorphism to `U`, so determinant invariance
under conjugacy gives `U.det = 1`.

The proof includes `n = 0`: then the bottom is also the top, so the ambient
module is subsingleton and the empty determinant product is one.  Empty
graded index types are harmless.  No field hypothesis is used.

## API novelty

The closest existing APIs are:

* `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStage_castSucc` and
  `Module.Basis.ofFiltrationStageVector_mk`, which provide the exact basis
  representatives but do not prove stability of an arbitrary endomorphism;
* `LinearMap.det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton`, which factors a
  determinant once invariant stages and quotient maps are already supplied;
* matrix triangular determinant lemmas, which would require an additional
  order on the dependent basis index and would duplicate the filtration
  infrastructure.

The theorem below is therefore the missing bridge: it derives both stage
stability and graded identity from the basis-level error hypothesis.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open Module
open scoped BigOperators

universe uR uM uι

namespace Module.Basis

variable {R : Type uR} {M : Type uM} [CommRing R]
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
variable {κ : ℕ → Type uι}

/-- Passing an early filtration basis vector through any number of later
stages does not change its underlying ambient value. -/
private theorem coe_ofFiltrationStage_eq_of_le
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ n) (i : Fin j) (a : κ i.val) :
    ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ j
        (fun k => hF (k.castLE hj))
        (fun k => b (k.castLE hj)) ⟨i, a⟩ : F j) : M) =
      ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n hF b
        ⟨i.castLE hj, a⟩ : F n) : M) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => exact Fin.elim0 (i.castLE hj)
  | succ n ih =>
      by_cases hjn : j ≤ n
      · calc
          _ = ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ n
                (fun k => hF k.castSucc)
                (fun k => b k.castSucc)
                ⟨i.castLE hjn, a⟩ : F n) : M) :=
            ih (fun k => hF k.castSucc) (fun k => b k.castSucc) hjn
          _ = ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ (n + 1) hF b
                ⟨i.castLE hj, a⟩ : F (n + 1)) : M) := by
            symm
            simpa using ofFiltrationStage_castSucc F hzero κ n hF b
              (i.castLE hjn) a
      · have hjeq : j = n + 1 := by omega
        subst j
        rfl

private theorem filtration_mono_of_succ
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≤ j) (hj : j ≤ n) : F i ≤ F j := by
  revert hj
  refine Nat.le_induction (m := i)
    (P := fun j _ => j ≤ n → F i ≤ F j) ?_ ?_ j hij
  · intro _
    exact le_rfl
  · intro k hik ih hk1n
    exact (ih (Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ k) hk1n)).trans
      (hF ⟨k, Nat.lt_of_succ_le hk1n⟩)

/-- A vector in a prefix filtration basis agrees in `M` with the
corresponding vector of the final assembled basis. -/
theorem ofFiltration_apply_eq_ofFiltrationStage
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤)
    {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ n) (i : Fin j) (a : κ i.val) :
    ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i.castLE hj, a⟩ =
      ((ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ j
        (fun k => hF (k.castLE hj))
        (fun k => b (k.castLE hj)) ⟨i, a⟩ : F j) : M) := by
  rw [ofFiltration_apply]
  exact (coe_ofFiltrationStage_eq_of_le F hzero n hF b hj i a).symm

/-- The basis-level condition `U b - b ∈ F i` on every vector introduced at
grade `i` forces every filtration stage to be `U`-stable. -/
theorem ofFiltration_stable
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤)
    (U : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (hU : ∀ i : Fin n, ∀ a : κ i.val,
      U (ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i, a⟩) -
          ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i, a⟩ ∈ F i.val)
    [∀ i : Fin n, Finite (κ i.val)]
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ n) : F j ≤ (F j).comap U := by
  let _ : ∀ i : Fin n, Fintype (κ i.val) := fun _ => Fintype.ofFinite _
  let _ : ∀ i : Fin j, Fintype (κ i.val) := fun i =>
    inferInstanceAs (Fintype (κ (i.castLE hj).val))
  let bj := ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ j
    (fun k => hF (k.castLE hj)) (fun k => b (k.castLE hj))
  intro x hx
  let xj : F j := ⟨x, hx⟩
  have hsum := bj.sum_repr xj
  have hsumM := congrArg (fun z : F j => (z : M)) hsum
  have hcoe :
      (((∑ p, (bj.repr xj) p • bj p : F j) : F j) : M) =
        ∑ p, (bj.repr xj) p • (bj p : M) := by
    change (F j).subtype (∑ p, (bj.repr xj) p • bj p) = _
    rw [map_sum]
    simp only [map_smul]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro p _
    rfl
  have hsumM' :
      (∑ p, (bj.repr xj) p • (bj p : M)) = (xj : M) :=
    hcoe.symm.trans hsumM
  change U (xj : M) ∈ F j
  rw [← hsumM', map_sum]
  exact Submodule.sum_mem _ fun p _ => by
    rw [map_smul]
    apply Submodule.smul_mem
    have hpref := ofFiltration_apply_eq_ofFiltrationStage
      F hzero n hF b htop hj p.1 p.2
    have herr := hU (p.1.castLE hj) p.2
    rw [hpref] at herr
    have herrj : U (bj p : M) - (bj p : M) ∈ F j :=
      filtration_mono_of_succ F n hF (Nat.le_of_lt p.1.isLt) hj herr
    rw [← sub_add_cancel (U (bj p : M)) (bj p : M)]
    exact Submodule.add_mem _ herrj (bj p).property

end Module.Basis

namespace LinearMap

open Module.Basis

variable {R : Type uR} {M : Type uM} [CommRing R]
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
variable {κ : ℕ → Type uι}

/-- An endomorphism that fixes each assembled filtration-basis vector modulo
the preceding filtration stage has determinant one.  Stage stability and
identity on the successive quotients are conclusions of the proof, not
inputs. -/
theorem det_eq_one_of_sub_mem_ofFiltration
    (F : ℕ → Submodule R M) (hzero : F 0 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ)
    (hF : ∀ i : Fin n, F i.val ≤ F (i.val + 1))
    (b : ∀ i : Fin n,
      Basis (κ i.val) R
        (F (i.val + 1) ⧸ (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype))
    (htop : F n = ⊤)
    (U : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (hU : ∀ i : Fin n, ∀ a : κ i.val,
      U (ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i, a⟩) -
          ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop ⟨i, a⟩ ∈ F i.val)
    [∀ i : Fin n, Finite (κ i.val)] :
    U.det = 1 := by
  let _ : ∀ i : Fin n, Fintype (κ i.val) := fun _ => Fintype.ofFinite _
  let B := ofFiltration F hzero κ n hF b htop
  let _ : Module.Free R M := Module.Free.of_basis B
  let _ : Module.Finite R M := Module.Finite.of_basis B
  let stageLE : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), j.val ≤ n := fun j =>
    Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp j.isLt
  let stageBasis (j : Fin (n + 1)) :
      Basis (FiltrationIndex κ j.val) R (F j.val) :=
    ofFiltrationStage F hzero κ j.val
      (fun k => hF (k.castLE (stageLE j)))
      (fun k => b (k.castLE (stageLE j)))
  let _ : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Fintype (FiltrationIndex κ j.val) := fun j => by
    let _ : ∀ i : Fin j.val, Fintype (κ i.val) := fun i =>
      inferInstanceAs (Fintype (κ (i.castLE (stageLE j)).val))
    infer_instance
  let _ : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Module.Free R (F j.val) := fun j =>
    Module.Free.of_basis (stageBasis j)
  let _ : ∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Module.Finite R (F j.val) := fun j =>
    Module.Finite.of_basis (stageBasis j)
  let stable (j : Fin (n + 1)) : F j.val ≤ (F j.val).comap U :=
    ofFiltration_stable F hzero n hF b htop U hU j.val (stageLE j)
  let endomorphism (j : Fin (n + 1)) : F j.val →ₗ[R] F j.val :=
    U.restrict (stable j)
  let step (i : Fin n) :
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ) :=
    { submodule := (F i.val).comap (F (i.val + 1)).subtype
      stable := by
        intro x hx
        change U (x : M) ∈ F i.val
        exact stable i.castSucc hx
      equiv := (Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe (hF i)).symm
      intertwines := by
        apply LinearMap.ext
        intro x
        rfl }
  have hquotient (i : Fin n) :
      (step i).quotientMap = LinearMap.id := by
    apply (b i).ext
    intro a
    rw [← ofFiltrationStageVector_mk F hzero κ n hF b i a]
    rw [InvariantExtension.quotientMap_mk]
    apply (Submodule.Quotient.eq _).mpr
    change U
        ((ofFiltrationStageVector F hzero κ n hF b i a : F (i.val + 1)) : M) -
      ((ofFiltrationStageVector F hzero κ n hF b i a : F (i.val + 1)) : M) ∈
        F i.val
    simpa only [ofFiltrationStageVector, ofFiltration_apply] using hU i a
  let _ : Subsingleton (F (0 : Fin (n + 1)).val) := by
    change Subsingleton (F 0)
    rw [hzero]
    infer_instance
  have hdetStage : (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det = 1 := by
    rw [det_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton
      endomorphism step (fun i => Module.Free.of_basis (b i))]
    simp only [hquotient, LinearMap.det_id, Finset.prod_const_one]
  let eTop : F n ≃ₗ[R] M :=
    (LinearEquiv.ofEq (F n) ⊤ htop).trans Submodule.topEquiv
  have hconj : eTop.conj (endomorphism (Fin.last n)) = U := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro x
    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := eTop.surjective x
    rfl
  calc
    U.det = (eTop.conj (endomorphism (Fin.last n))).det := by rw [hconj]
    _ = (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).det := by
      change LinearMap.det
          (((eTop : F n →ₗ[R] M) ∘ₗ endomorphism (Fin.last n)) ∘ₗ
            (eTop.symm : M →ₗ[R] F n)) =
        LinearMap.det (endomorphism (Fin.last n))
      exact LinearMap.det_conj (endomorphism (Fin.last n)) eTop
    _ = 1 := hdetStage

end LinearMap

end

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.ToMatrix
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Charpoly.Basic
public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Determinant.FiniteFiltration

/-!
# Characteristic polynomials along finite invariant filtrations

This file is the characteristic-polynomial analogue of
`MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Determinant.FiniteFiltration`.  It packages and
iterates the characteristic-polynomial factorization for an endomorphism
preserving a submodule, for finite filtrations whose stages and successive
quotients are finite free modules.

## Main declarations

* `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_one_of_subsingleton` computes the characteristic
  polynomial on a zero module.
* `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly` is the raw one-step
  factorization for an invariant submodule, the characteristic-polynomial
  analogue of Mathlib's `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det`.
* `LinearMap.InvariantExtension.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly_quotientMap`
  is the one-step factorization packaged by an invariant extension.
* `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_prod_graded` iterates the factorization
  through a finite tower.
* `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton` removes the
  bottom factor when the initial stage is zero.

## Informal proof

For one step, choose a basis of the invariant submodule `S` and a basis of
`W / S`, and combine them into a basis of `W` with `Module.Basis.sumQuot`.
Exactly as in Mathlib's proof of `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det`, the matrix
of the endomorphism in this basis is block upper-triangular, with diagonal
blocks the matrices of the restriction and of the quotient map.  The matrix
characteristic polynomial of a block upper-triangular matrix is the product
of the characteristic polynomials of its diagonal blocks
(`Matrix.charpoly_fromBlocks_zero₂₁`), which gives the raw factorization.

The stored intertwining equality in an invariant extension says that the
restriction is conjugate to the lower-stage endomorphism, and characteristic
polynomials are invariant under conjugation, giving the packaged one-step
formula.  The finite-tower formula is then the same `Fin n` induction as in
the determinant file: if `p_{i+1} = p_i * q_i`, then
`p_n = p_0 * ∏ i, q_i`.  When the bottom stage is a zero module, its
characteristic polynomial is `1` (the empty matrix), leaving only the
product over the graded quotients.

The freeness of every successive quotient is explicit, as in the determinant
file: over an arbitrary commutative ring it does not follow merely from
freeness of the two adjacent stages.  The upper stage is also assumed free;
unlike `LinearMap.det`, the characteristic polynomial is only defined on
finite free modules.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped BigOperators
open Polynomial

universe u v w

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
variable {V : Type v} {W : Type w}
variable [AddCommGroup V] [Module R V]
variable [AddCommGroup W] [Module R W]

/-- The characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism of a zero module is
`1`, paralleling `LinearMap.det_eq_one_of_subsingleton`. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_one_of_subsingleton {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Module.Free R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Subsingleton M]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] M) : f.charpoly = 1 := by
  have b : Module.Basis (Fin 0) R M := Module.Basis.empty M
  rw [← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix f b]
  exact Matrix.charpoly_isEmpty

open Module.Basis in
/-- Characteristic-polynomial factorization for an endomorphism preserving
a submodule: the characteristic polynomial is the product of those of the
restriction and of the induced quotient map.  This is the
characteristic-polynomial analogue of `LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_det`, with
the same block upper-triangular matrix proof. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly (e : W →ₗ[R] W) (S : Submodule R W)
    (he : S ≤ S.comap e) [Module.Free R W] [Module.Finite R W]
    [Module.Free R S] [Module.Finite R S] [Module.Free R (W ⧸ S)] :
    e.charpoly = (e.restrict he).charpoly * (S.mapQ S e he).charpoly := by
  let m := Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex R S
  let bW : Module.Basis m R S := Module.Free.chooseBasis R S
  let n := Module.Free.ChooseBasisIndex R (W ⧸ S)
  let bQ : Module.Basis n R (W ⧸ S) := Module.Free.chooseBasis R (W ⧸ S)
  let b := sumQuot bW bQ
  let A : Matrix m m R := LinearMap.toMatrix bW bW (e.restrict he)
  let B : Matrix m n R := Matrix.of fun i l ↦
    ((sumQuot bW bQ).repr (e ((sumQuot bW bQ) (Sum.inr l)))) (Sum.inl i)
  let D : Matrix n n R := LinearMap.toMatrix bQ bQ (S.mapQ S e he)
  suffices LinearMap.toMatrix b b e = Matrix.fromBlocks A B 0 D by
    rw [← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix e b, this,
      ← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ bW, ← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ bQ,
      Matrix.charpoly_fromBlocks_zero₂₁]
  ext u v
  cases u with
  | inl i =>
    cases v with
    | inl k =>
      simp only [b, sumQuot_inl, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₁, A,
        LinearMap.toMatrix_apply]
      apply sumQuot_repr_inl_of_mem
    | inr l => simp [b, LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₁₂, B]
  | inr j =>
    cases v with
    | inl k =>
      suffices S.mkQ (e (bW k)) = 0 by simp [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, b, this]
      rw [← LinearMap.mem_ker, Submodule.ker_mkQ]
      exact he (Submodule.coe_mem (bW k))
    | inr l =>
      simp only [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, sumQuot_repr_inr,
        Matrix.fromBlocks_apply₂₂, b, D]
      rw [← sumQuot_inr bW bQ l, S.mapQ_apply]
      simp

namespace InvariantExtension

variable {f : V →ₗ[R] V} {g : W →ₗ[R] W}

/-- Characteristic-polynomial factorization for one invariant extension.

This is the reusable one-step block-triangular formula, the
characteristic-polynomial analogue of
`LinearMap.InvariantExtension.det_eq_det_mul_det_quotientMap`.  The upper
stage is assumed free because `LinearMap.charpoly`, unlike `LinearMap.det`,
is only defined on finite free modules. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly_quotientMap
    (E : InvariantExtension f g) [Module.Free R V] [Module.Finite R V]
    [Module.Free R W] [Module.Finite R W]
    [Module.Free R (W ⧸ E.submodule)] :
    g.charpoly = f.charpoly * E.quotientMap.charpoly := by
  let _ : Module.Free R E.submodule := Module.Free.of_equiv E.equiv
  let _ : Module.Finite R E.submodule := Module.Finite.equiv E.equiv
  calc
    g.charpoly = (g.restrict E.stable).charpoly * E.quotientMap.charpoly :=
      g.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly E.submodule E.stable
    _ = f.charpoly * E.quotientMap.charpoly := by
      rw [← E.conjugate_eq]
      congr 1
      simpa only [LinearEquiv.conj_apply, LinearMap.comp_assoc] using
        (LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj E.equiv f)

end InvariantExtension

private theorem charpoly_last_eq_first_mul_prod {n : ℕ}
    (d : Fin (n + 1) → R[X]) (q : Fin n → R[X])
    (h : ∀ i, d i.succ = d i.castSucc * q i) :
    d (Fin.last n) = d 0 * ∏ i, q i := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      have hprefix :
          d (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) =
            d 0 * ∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc := by
        apply ih (d := fun i ↦ d i.castSucc) (q := fun i ↦ q i.castSucc)
        intro i
        simpa using h i.castSucc
      calc
        d (Fin.last (n + 1)) =
            d (Fin.castSucc (Fin.last n)) * q (Fin.last n) := by
          simpa using h (Fin.last n)
        _ = (d 0 * ∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc) * q (Fin.last n) := by
          rw [hprefix]
        _ = d 0 * ((∏ i : Fin n, q i.castSucc) * q (Fin.last n)) := by
          rw [mul_assoc]
        _ = d 0 * ∏ i, q i := by
          rw [Fin.prod_univ_castSucc]

section FiniteTower

variable {n : ℕ} {M : Fin (n + 1) → Type v}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- The characteristic polynomial on the final stage of a finite invariant
filtration is the characteristic polynomial on the initial stage times the
product of the characteristic polynomials on all successive graded
quotients.  This is the characteristic-polynomial analogue of
`LinearMap.det_eq_det_mul_prod_graded`, with the same interface: each
`step i` identifies stage `i` with an invariant submodule of stage `i+1`. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_prod_graded
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule)) :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).charpoly =
      (endomorphism 0).charpoly * ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.charpoly := by
  refine charpoly_last_eq_first_mul_prod
    (d := fun i ↦ (endomorphism i).charpoly)
    (q := fun i ↦ (step i).quotientMap.charpoly) ?_
  intro i
  let _ : Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule) := quotientFree i
  exact (step i).charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_charpoly_quotientMap

/-- Version of `LinearMap.charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_prod_graded` for a
filtration whose bottom characteristic polynomial has already been
identified with one. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_charpoly_eq_one
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule))
    (hbottom : (endomorphism 0).charpoly = 1) :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.charpoly := by
  rw [charpoly_eq_charpoly_mul_prod_graded endomorphism step quotientFree,
    hbottom, one_mul]

/-- Characteristic-polynomial product formula for a finite invariant
filtration starting at a zero module. -/
theorem charpoly_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_subsingleton
    (endomorphism : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i)
    (step : ∀ i : Fin n,
      InvariantExtension (endomorphism i.castSucc) (endomorphism i.succ))
    (quotientFree : ∀ i, Module.Free R (M i.succ ⧸ (step i).submodule))
    [Subsingleton (M 0)] :
    (endomorphism (Fin.last n)).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (step i).quotientMap.charpoly :=
  charpoly_eq_prod_graded_of_bottom_charpoly_eq_one endomorphism step
    quotientFree (LinearMap.charpoly_eq_one_of_subsingleton _)

end FiniteTower

end LinearMap
